Server's reverse proxy trust: the providers' saved lists are read and written async under the caller's token. Configure is async (the server's configure awaits it) and reads a new provider's file before taking its lock, where a list fetched meanwhile wins over the older file; the read was sync inside the lock. The write goes through FileUtils.WriteAllTextAtomicAsync, under the refresh's token, with a temporary file of its own name that a failure removes; it was sync, through a fixed .tmp that a failure left behind. A failed write has its own log line - the fetched list is in use, and the next start reads the last list kept - where it was logged as a failed refresh whose last list stood Tested: the whole VpnHood.Test (but two PacketChannel_max_upload timings, which failed under load and passed alone three times) with a new test - a failed write leaves the fetched list in use and no temporary file - and the whole VpnHood.AppLib.Test (but VpnTunnelLockTest's three, which another app's tunnel lock fails here).

iOS: an app updated while connected opens on Disconnected, not on "VPN service encountered an issue". iOS ends the VPN extension without a word to it for an update, so the status the extension left still says connected and the app found no running service. Where none runs, the app now asks iOS how the session ended (NEVPNConnection.fetchLastDisconnectError, in IosVpnServiceEnd): no error is a session that ended (VpnServiceNotReadyException, as Android's AndroidVpnServiceEnd); an error - a crash or a kill for memory, NEVPNConnectionErrorDomain 12 - keeps the dialog. iOS 15, which keeps no such error, takes every end as a session that ended. The CHANGELOG line joins Android's.
